answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each agent's influence cost something real and verifiable, like staking earned reputation on a shared ledge of past attestations. New identities must accumulate trust slowly, the way a mesa forms layer by layer, while existing peers randomly audit claims before countersigning them. An ivory-tower scheme that only counts raw accounts fails; tying weight to work history, staked value, and peer attestation makes flooding the economy with fake agents expensive and detectable.
